title: ouch
expanded:
==English== ===Etymology 1=== Uncertain[[Category:English terms with unknown etymologies|OUCH]]. Some sources say the interjection is attested since 1838{{R:MWO}} (and specifically in American English) and derives ultimately from [[w:German language|German]][[Category:English terms derived from German|OUCH]] [[:autsch#German|autsch]],{{R:Dictionary.com}}{{R:New English Dictionary}} ([https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.99996/page/n521 "ouch"]) perhaps specifically via [[w:Pennsylvania Dutch language|Pennsylvania German]][[Category:English terms derived from Pennsylvania German|OUCH]] [[:outch#Pennsylvania_German|outch]] (“cry of pain”), as early attestations of the interjection are from Pennsylvania. However, others say the interjection is a "mere"{{R:Century}} or "natural" exclamation attested since the mid 1600s,{{R:Lexico}} and the 1933 ''OED'' cites one instance of a ''verb'' "ouch" in 1654, "Sancho Pancas Runs Ouching round the mountaine like a ranck-Asse".'''1654''', Gayton, ''Pleas. Notes'' IV. ii. 176, "But harke Sancho Pancas Runs Ouching round the mountaine like a ranck-Asse, Braying for's Company. ====Pronunciation==== * [[Wiktionary:International Phonetic Alphabet|IPA]]([[Appendix:English pronunciation|key]]): /aʊt͡ʃ/[[Category:English 1-syllable words|OUCH]][[Category:English terms with IPA pronunciation|OUCH]] * Rhymes: [[Rhymes:English/aʊtʃ|-aʊtʃ]][[Category:Rhymes:English/aʊtʃ|OUCH]][[Category:Rhymes:English/aʊtʃ/1 syllable|OUCH]] *
Audio ([[w:American English|US]], [[w:Inland Northern American English|Inland Northern American]]):[[File:en-us-inlandnorth-ouch.ogg|noicon|175px]]([[:File:en-us-inlandnorth-ouch.ogg|file]])
[[Category:English terms with audio pronunciation|OUCH]] ====Interjection==== ouch[[Category:English lemmas|OUCH]][[Category:English interjections|OUCH]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|OUCH]][[Category:Pages with entries|OUCH]][[Category:Pages with 3 entries|OUCH]] # An expression of one's own physical [[pain]]. #:
'''Ouch'''! You stepped on my toe! That hurt!
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|OUCH]] # An expression in [[sympathy]] at another's pain. #:
'''Ouch'''! Her sunburn looks awful.
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|OUCH]] # A reply to an [[insult]] seen as savage (frequently one that is [[tongue-in-cheek]] or joking). #:
'''Ouch'''. How could you say that?
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|OUCH]] # An expression of disappointment. #:
'''Ouch''', I really wanted to do that.
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|OUCH]] # ([[Appendix:Glossary#slang|slang]][[Category:English slang|OUCH]]) Expressing surprise at the high [[price]] of something. #:
'''Ouch''', one hundred thousand dollars for a car! I could never afford that!
